subject: feat(loop-video): 末尾に CRF 圧縮ステップを追加し本編動画容量を約 40% 削減 (#175)
message:
feat(loop-video): 末尾に CRF 圧縮ステップを追加し本編動画容量を約 40% 削減 (#175)

Veo 3.1 由来の loop.mp4 は 1080p / 24fps / H.264 で 5.6〜6.0 Mbps あり、
generate_videos.sh が stream copy で本編動画を組むため最終マスター動画も
そのビットレートを継承し、2h 30m 級コレクションで 6.8〜7.8 GB に肥大化していた。
YouTube は受信動画を VP9/AV1 に再 transcoding するため、CRF 22 程度の
再圧縮では視聴品質に有意な影響は出ない。

veo_generator.compress_loop(crf, preset) を新規追加し、Veo 出力直後に
libx264 で再エンコードする。compression が有効なときは strip_audio の
stream copy パスを skip して ffmpeg 起動を 1 回に集約。
smooth_loop も crf/preset を引数化し、--smooth 経路でも同じ設定を
継承して圧縮効果が巻き戻らないようにした。

skill-config の compression.{enabled,crf,preset} で上書き可能で、
既定は CRF 22 / preset slow（約 40% 削減）。channel 側で CRF 24 に
攻めれば約 55% 削減も可能（要 A/B 比較）。generate_videos.sh 側は
stream copy 設計を維持し既存マスター動画は触らない。

Closes #175

Veo 3.1 は課金 API でデフォルト経路は既存 loop.mp4 を退避してから
新規 Veo を叩く（フル再課金）ため、Quick Reference テーブルと
新規「再実行時のコスト警告」セクションに以下を明文化した:

- 既存 loop.mp4 がある状態での挙動マトリクス（素実行 / --skip-existing /
  --smooth / 両方併用の 4 行で Veo 呼び出し有無と課金を表形式で提示）
- 冪等再実行は --skip-existing で既存があれば early exit 0（0 円 no-op）
- 継ぎ目補正は --smooth 単独 mode（FFmpeg post-process 専用、Veo を叩かず 0 円）

subject: refactor(skills): add inline protocol summaries and attention anchoring to all skill prompts
message:
refactor(skills): add inline protocol summaries and attention anchoring to all skill prompts

## What Changed
- 233 SKILL.md files refactored with two structural improvements
- 2 hook files (knowledge-context.cjs, subagent-init.cjs) updated with same pattern
- Template skill updated to document new pattern for future skill creation
- Reusable refactoring script added (.claude/scripts/refactor-skill-prompts.py)

## Why — The AI Attention Problem
LLM attention is strongest at the TOP and BOTTOM of a prompt, weakest in the
middle. Our skill prompts had two issues causing AI to skip critical protocols:

1. **Bare "MUST READ file.md" instructions** — AI frequently skipped reading
   external protocol files entirely, leading to protocol violations (no evidence
   citations, skipped investigation steps, rationalization of shortcuts). The AI
   would see "MUST READ" but treat it as optional since the protocol content was
   not visible in the current context.

2. **No bottom anchoring** — Critical rules stated only at the top were forgotten
   by the time AI reached the middle/end of long skill prompts, causing drift
   from key constraints during execution.

## What Improved

### Inline Protocol Summaries (218 replacements)
Every "MUST READ `shared/protocol.md`" reference now includes a 2-3 line inline
summary of the protocol's core rules BEFORE the read instruction:

  Before: `**MUST READ** \`.claude/skills/shared/evidence-based-reasoning-protocol.md\``
  After:  `> **Evidence-Based Reasoning** — Speculation is FORBIDDEN. Every claim
           needs file:line proof. Confidence >95% recommend freely, 80-94% with
           caveats, <80% DO NOT recommend.
           > MUST READ \`path\` for full protocol and checklists.`

This ensures AI absorbs the key rules even if it doesn't read the full file,
while still directing it to the complete protocol for detailed steps.

Protocols covered: understand-code-first, evidence-based-reasoning,
rationalization-prevention, red-flag-stop-conditions, graph-assisted-investigation,
ui-system-context, iterative-phase-quality, plan-quality, two-stage-review,
estimation-framework, design-patterns-quality, double-round-trip-review, and more.

### Bottom Attention Anchoring (218 Closing Reminders sections)
Standardized "## Closing Reminders" section added to the bottom of every
content skill, reinforcing the most critical rules:
- Break work into small tasks (TaskCreate)
- Search 3+ existing patterns before creating new code
- Cite file:line evidence for every claim
- Add final review task

### Scope Discipline
- Only .claude/ protocol files got inline summaries
- Project-specific docs (docs/project-reference/*) correctly left as plain
  read instructions since their content varies per project

## Principles Applied
- **Attention Anchoring**: Key rules at both top AND bottom of prompts
- **Progressive Disclosure**: Summary first, detailed file for deep-dive
- **DRY with intentional duplication**: Summaries duplicated across skills
  by design — each skill must be self-contained since AI loads them independently
- **Automation**: Script-based batch refactoring ensures consistency across 233 files

## Verification
- 300/300 hook tests pass
- Zero project-specific docs incorrectly summarized
- Zero formatting issues (list-to-blockquote gaps resolved)
- Template skill updated with new pattern

fix: [T622] restore the shared tree's task branch after the review-mode §7 gate

The review-mode [orchestrated run] (gate-loop) dispatches read-only auditor
subagents in the SHARED main working tree. Those agents have Bash, so a stray
`git checkout`/`git switch` in an auditor step silently relocates the maker's
HEAD off the task branch onto base (the #139 reflog drift) — stranding
uncommitted work or producing a push/PR from the wrong branch state.

The gate-loop runtime has no git access, so the deterministic restore lives in
the dispatcher and is bound by a new hook:

- NEW hooks/restore-task-branch.sh — no-op when HEAD is already on the task
  branch, restores via `git switch` when an auditor drifted it, fails LOUD
  (exit 1) when it cannot guarantee the branch (the deliberate inverse of the
  reconcile hooks' fail-open posture — a state-protection backstop must not
  green-light an unverified HEAD).
- NEW hooks/restore-task-branch.test.sh — real-git harness encoding the
  done-when criteria: DW1 (an auditor's switch DID drift HEAD — fail-before —
  and the helper restores it — pass-after, not a tautology), DW2 (after restore
  the auditors' NON-SWITCHING base reads still return correct base content), DW3
  (the restore is exercised after BOTH a PASS-outcome and a FAIL-outcome branch
  state); plus no-op, detached-HEAD, fail-loud, usage, and wiring assertions.
- ci.yml — wire the new test into `verify`.
- skills/next-task/SKILL.md — the dispatcher runs the restore after the gate
  returns (every outcome), before the telemetry `git rev-parse HEAD`, so a
  drifted HEAD can neither strand the maker nor poison the record.
- workflow/gate-loop.md — neutral, role-only: the dispatcher restores the
  shared-tree branch every outcome; reviewers use non-switching base reads.
- workflows/gate-loop.js (+ test) — append the non-switching base-read
  instruction to the reviewer prompt (the prevention layer; the restore is the
  deterministic backstop) and assert it ships.
- EXTRACTION.md — manifest rows + count for the two new hooks.

A guard rule blocking `git switch main` was rejected: it is textually identical
to the allowlisted post-merge step (AGENTS.md "After any merge, run

* fix: [T639] pin gate-diff to the verified SHA and gate the marker on diff success (#245 review)

pre-fix hook, all green after):
- a GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF driver that emits a partial patch then exits
  non-zero yields exit 1 + the mismatch marker and never the completion
  marker over the partial patch.
- source-level pin guards: the emission diffs `$branch_sha` and never
  re-resolves live HEAD (the TOCTOU race is not deterministically
  reproducible, so the property is pinned at the source).

Verified locally: full CI `verify` suite green (48 hook checks +
gate-loop.test.js 26 + omnigent py); shell-lint clean. gate-loop.js
unchanged — the classifier already fails closed on the mismatch marker.

subject: fix: [T642] gate-loop preflight — fail fast when reviewer agent types are unresolvable (#269)
message:
fix: [T642] gate-loop preflight — fail fast when reviewer agent types are unresolvable (#269)

* fix: [T642] preflight gate-loop reviewer agent types, abort fast when unresolvable

The [orchestrated run] dispatches reviewers by custom agentType, which the
runtime resolves from the dispatcher session root's .claude/agents/, NOT from
workspacePath. A dispatcher rooted outside the repo cannot resolve them, so
every reviewer dispatch returns NO-RESULT and the loop — correctly refusing to
pass — burns the whole max-fix-rounds budget grading nothing (issue #214:
9x NO-RESULT across 3 rounds, outcome non-convergence, zero grading).

Add a deterministic preflight before round 1: probe each distinct roster agent
type once; a null return (the same NO-RESULT the fan-out would get, paid once)
means unresolvable. On any unresolvable type, abort before any reviewer
dispatch — zero fix rounds — with a diagnostic derived from the actual
unresolved set that names the dispatcher-outside-repo cause. All-resolvable
runs proceed unchanged (two-sided).

Telemetry reuses outcome 'fail' with a preflight-keyed fail_reports entry,
mirroring the diff-provider abort precedent — no outcome-enum churn. Docs split
per constitution P1: gate-loop.md -> Inputs carries the neutral precondition;
the concrete agent-type-from-session-root fact lives in README + the next-task
SKILL [orchestrated run] rows. telemetry.md documents the new fail_reports key.

Encoded by gate-loop.test.js: an unresolvable-types case (RED against prior
behavior: fix_rounds_used==2, non-convergence; GREEN: aborts, fix_rounds_used==0,
diagnostic names types + cause) plus a resolvable control. Probe resolution is
modelled in the test harness so the 26 pre-T642 cases stay green untouched.

Closes #214

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: [T642] address PR #269 review — pass models to preflight probes; doc honesty

Codex P1 (guard rule 5): the preflight probed constitution-auditor /
spec-quality-auditor WITHOUT a `model`, but guard.sh rule 5 blocks a
strong-floored reviewer dispatched model-less (strong-floor-no-model). In a
guarded run the probe would be blocked and then MISREPORTED as an
unresolvable-agent abort. Fix: probe over the `reviewers` array (not deduped
keys) and pass `model: r.model` on each probe — exactly as the grading dispatch
does. Encoded by gate-loop.test.js test 29 (RED before: probes carried no

but an abort record (diff-provider / preflight) audits no diff. Clarify that on
an abort record (empty `rounds`) `commit` is the head that WOULD have been
audited, and the empty `rounds` is the disambiguator so Fact B never misreads it.

  typically piped/redirected) or an interactive prompt, so it never appears
  in argv. The `--mnemonic` flag still works for backward compatibility.

- Emit a runtime warning when `--mnemonic`/`--passphrase` are passed as flags.
- Docs (SKILL.md, references, usage) now show stdin/interactive/env/file
  methods and explicitly warn against argv; drop `--passphrase`/`--mnemonic`
  from documented commands. (Passphrase already resolved via env/file/prompt.)

subject: Update execution contract and skill guidelines to enforce "problem is fixed" default outcome
message:

This change affects every skill and agent by requiring them to pursue root causes fully, expand scope when needed, and avoid workarounds or dodging behaviors. New hooks enforce these rules at the tool use level, blocking forbidden commands and temp file policies. The skill documentation has been updated consistently across all skills to reflect this new discipline, removing allowances for stopping on uncertainty and emphasizing that low confidence means "read more" rather than "stop."
